newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher on light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $50.50 to $51.00.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $49.50 to $50.00, the dealers said. Indiana and Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50, they said.
Light marketings were attributed to producers' holding back of hogs following steep declines last week.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings on Friday were 85,000 head, compared with the estimate of 95,000, USDA said. Monday's receipts were estimated at 95,000 head, compared with 107,000 a week ago and 113,000 a year ago.
Light support also was expected from ideas that pork prices could be firm if production wanes, dealers said.
Pork cut-out values Friday were up $0.41 to $0.45 per cwt, USDA said.
Pork prices at midday, however, were not tested, except for hams, which were steady. There were 20.0 loads of pork cuts sold and 3.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
